in_sanskrit.name: अत्रि
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Atri is derived from the Sanskrit word अत्रि (Atri), which means 'boundless' or 'unending'. In Hindu mythology, Atri is the name of a sage and the father of the celestial nymphs, the Apsaras. He is also one of the seven great Rishis (sages) and is said to have performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva.

in_hindi.name: अट्री
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, the name Atri is transliterated as अट्री (Aṭrī). The meaning of the name in Hindi is 'beyond, more, endless'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word अत्रि (Atri), which means 'boundless' or 'unending'.

in_tamil.name: அத்ரி
in_tamil.long_meaning: In Tamil, the name Atri is transliterated as அத்ரி (Aṭri). The meaning of the name in Tamil is 'beyond, excessive, other'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word अत्रि (Atri), which means 'boundless' or 'unending'.

in_telugu.name: అత్రి
in_telugu.long_meaning: In Telugu, the name Atri is transliterated as అత్రి (Aṭri). The meaning of the name in Telugu is 'beyond, limitless, boundless'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word अत्रि (Atri), which means 'boundless' or 'unending'.

in_marathi.name: Atri
in_marathi.long_meaning: Atri हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। Atri is a Sanskrit name derived from the ancient Hindu text 'Mahabharata'. vedic_reference.note: Atri is a significant name in Hindu mythology and is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures. He is considered one of the seven great Rishis and is known for his penance and devotion to Lord Shiva. In the Vedas, Atri is mentioned as one of the sons of the sage Angiras and the goddess Svaha. He is also known as Atreya, and his hymns are found in the Rigveda.
